extracted.intended_audience: trademark examiners, intellectual property classifiers, and practitioners using the Vienna Classification to index/classify figurative elements of marks
extracted.subtask_description: Apply the Vienna Classification (5th edition) taxonomy to identify and assign figurative elements in marks/images to the correct categories and divisions; this chunk covers Categories 5 through 15 and their principal and auxiliary sections. Useful for indexing, searching, and examining trademark figurative components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 5 — PLANTS, FLOWERS, TREES, LEAVES, BRANCHES
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 5 covers flowers, plants, trees, leaves, branches, and related plant groups and arrangements (stylized flowers, single flowers, several flowers, bunches, sheaves, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes auxiliary sections (e.g., A 5.5.20 Stylized flowers; A 5.5.21 One flower; A 5.5.22 Several flowers) and many specific subdivisions for flowers, bunches, bowls or baskets of flowers. Notes specify exclusions such as surfaces or backgrounds covered with a repeated figurative element composed of flowers (placed in Category 25, e.g., 25.7.25). Where items are described as 'including' (e.g., cotton bolls), those examples clarify scope. Auxiliary sections are associated with specific principal sections and should be used to refine classification (e.g., A 5.x entries for single specimens or arrangements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 5.7 — GRAIN, SEEDS, FRUITS
rubrics_metrics.description: Division 5.7 enumerates grain, seeds and a wide range of fruits and fruit-related presentations (ears/panicles/sheaves of cereals, shell/husk fruits, cupulate fruits, small berries, grapes, citrus, apples, stone fruits, pears, cherries, pineapples, bananas, olives, melons, groups of fruits, bowls or baskets of fruit, fruits in jars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes include specific inclusions (e.g., coffee beans, cotton bolls) and exclusions (some cross-references to other sections). Principal sections include specific fruit types (e.g., 5.7.10 Grapes, 5.7.11 Oranges/mandarins/grapefruit, 5.7.19 Olives). Auxiliary sections refine presentation (e.g., A 5.7.22 Open fruits, slices or quarters; A 5.7.23 One fruit). Use the more specific auxiliary/principal section when the depiction matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 5.9 — VEGETABLES
rubrics_metrics.description: Division 5.9 covers vegetables and related plant-food items (carrots, potatoes and other tubers, onions/bulbs including garlic, leeks, asparagus, cabbages/lettuce/chicory, gourds, tomatoes, aubergines, beans/peas/lentils, baskets of vegetables, vegetables in jars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes cross-references and exclusions (e.g., lettuce prepared for immediate consumption is classified in 8.7.7). Principal and auxiliary sections allow classification at different specificity levels (e.g., A 5.9.23 One vegetable; 5.9.24 Groups of vegetables of different kinds). Use notes to avoid misclassification with food-preparation divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 5.11 — OTHER PLANTS
rubrics_metrics.description: Division 5.11 comprises other plant types not covered elsewhere: algae, seaweeds, roots/radicles/ginsengs, mosses, lichens, mushrooms, grasses, bamboo, reeds, sugar canes, maize canes, vanilla pods, potato seedlings, cotton plants, cones (fir/hop), agaves/aloes, prickly pears, cactus, plants in pots/ornamental stands/window-boxes/tubs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections (A 5.11.x) list many specific plant forms. Notes indicate inclusions (e.g., bamboo shoots included) and help decide placement when several plant types are present. Use auxiliary sections to represent presentation (potted plants, seedlings) or special material/parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 5.13 — DECORATIONS MADE OF PLANTS
rubrics_metrics.description: Division 5.13 covers plant-based decorations (crowns of leaves/flowers/fruits, crossed palms/branches, vine-branch decorations, garlands/bands/borders/frames made of plants, Christmas trees, other plant decorations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes state exclusions (e.g., vine shoots in 5.3.19; bunches of leaves in 5.3.16; bunches/sheaves of flowers 5.5.23; bowls/baskets of fruits 5.7.25; repeated figurative-pattern backgrounds in 25.7.25). Auxiliary sections (A 5.13.8–A 5.13.11) subdivide garlands/bands by material: leaves, flowers, fruits, or other plants. Use these when the decoration's constituent elements are identifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 6 — LANDSCAPES
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 6 covers landscape depictions, including mountains/rocks/grottoes, landscapes with water (rivers/streams, lacustrine/maritime scenes), desert/tropical-type landscapes, urban landscapes or village scenes, and other landscapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions specify types (e.g., 6.1 Mountains, rocks, grottoes; 6.3 Landscapes with water; 6.6 Desert or tropical-type; 6.7 Urban landscapes; 6.19 Other landscapes). Auxiliary sections refine to stylized forms (A 6.1.4 Mountains or volcanoes stylized), specific features (beaches, islands, reefs, harbors, waterfalls, springs) and built-up area compositions (skyscrapers, huts, rural constructions). Notes provide exclusions (e.g., reefs are in 6.3.1; urban scenes with water must be placed in 6.7.11). Guidance also clarifies forest vs. group-of-trees placement (e.g., group of three or more trees vs. forest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 7 — CONSTRUCTIONS, STRUCTURES FOR ADVERTISEMENTS, GATES OR BARRIERS
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 7 includes dwellings/buildings/advertisement hoardings/pillars/cages, parts of dwellings/buildings and interiors, monuments/stadiums/fountains, structural works (bridges, tunnels, roads, dams), and building materials/walls/gates/scaffolding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal sections list specific structures (castles, churches, mosques, pagodas, towers, houses, windmills, industrial establishments, advertisement hoardings, kiosks, huts, tents, igloos, animal cages). Notes clarify inclusions (e.g., transmitting masts) and exclusions (e.g., Eiffel Tower referenced separately). Auxiliary sections subdivide by typology (rural houses, flat-roofed houses, dwellings in ruins) and interior parts (doors, windows, kitchens, bathrooms). Building materials section (7.15) contains representations of stone, planks, corrugated materials and wood; notes state that representation of wood as ornamental background may be placed in Category 25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 8 — FOODSTUFFS
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 8 covers food items and presentations: bakers' products/pastry/confectionery/chocolate, milk/dairy/cheeses, butchers' meat/pork/fishmonger products, and other foodstuffs (soups, beverages, pasta, pizzas, salads, eggs, desserts, sugar, pet food).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal and auxiliary sections enumerate specific food types and presentations (e.g., bread, croissants, biscuits, slabs/sticks/squares of chocolate, milk/cream/butter/cheeses, ham/sausages/poultry/fish, soups/pizzas/dishes, mixtures of foodstuffs). Notes include inclusions (wafer cones, chewing gum) and cross-references to avoid misplacing food items that are ingredients vs. prepared-food depictions (e.g., lettuce prepared for immediate consumption in 8.7.7). Use auxiliary sections to classify specific shapes/presentations (e.g., slabs of chocolate, cheeses cut up).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 9 — TEXTILES, CLOTHING, SEWING ACCESSORIES, HEADWEAR, FOOTWEAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 9 comprises textiles (threads, laces, cloth, carpets, bed coverings), clothing and its parts (jackets, trousers, dresses, underwear), sewing accessories/patterns (needles, thimbles, buttons), headwear (turbans, caps, helmets), and footwear (clogs, shoes, boots, slippers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes indicate exclusions to prevent overlap (e.g., headwear is 9.7, footwear 9.9; fastening hooks and buttons cross-reference 9.5). Auxiliary sections provide fine-grained distinctions (thread presentations A 9.1.2–A 9.1.6; specific clothing parts and groups A 9.3.x; buttons/press-studs A 9.5.12–A 9.5.13; headwear auxiliaries A 9.7.2–A 9.7.25; footwear auxiliaries A 9.9.2–A 9.9.17). Use notes to guide placement of patterned/presentation variants (e.g., patterns resembling clothing placed in 9.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 10 — TOBACCO, SMOKERS' REQUISITES, MATCHES, TRAVEL GOODS, FANS, TOILET ARTICLES, MIRRORS
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 10 covers tobacco and smokers' requisites (tobacco, cigars, pipes, lighters, ash trays, matches), travel goods/fans/bags/umbrellas, and toilet articles and mirrors (toothbrushes, shaving articles, hair clippers, combs, lipsticks, mirrors, soap, sprays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections detail subtypes (pipes A 10.1.11, hookahs A 10.1.12, bags/suitcases A 10.3.10 with auxiliaries A 10.3.11–A 10.3.16 for shopping bags, satchels, rucksacks, suitcases). Notes flag exclusions (e.g., mirrors used in medicine in 19.13.1; sponges and packaging cross-references). Use the listed auxiliaries when the depiction is a particular accessory type (e.g., cigarette holders, cigar cutters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 11–15 — HOUSEHOLD UTENSILS; FURNITURE & SANITARY INSTALLATIONS; LIGHTING & APPLIANCES; IRONMONGERY, TOOLS, LADDERS; MACHINERY, MOTORS, ENGINES
rubrics_metrics.description: These categories cover (11) household utensils (knives, forks, spoons, kitchen utensils, containers, brushes, brooms), (12) furniture and sanitary installations (beds, chairs, tables, washbasins, baths), (13) lighting/wireless valves/heating/cooking/refrigerating/washing/drying equipment (candles, lamps, washing machines, ovens), (14) ironmongery/tools/agricultural implements/ladders (tubes, cables, nails, screws, keys, hammers, axes, spades, ladders), and (15) machinery, motors and engines (industrial machines, motors, propellers, parts, conveyors, household machines, spinning wheels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each division provides principal sections and extensive auxiliary sections for specific items and presentations (e.g., 11.1 utensils and 11.3 containers/dishes; 12.1 furniture with auxiliaries for beds, chairs, tables; 13.1 lighting with auxiliaries for lamps/lampshades and 13.3 heating/cooking appliances with auxiliaries for boilers, stoves, parts; 14.1 heavy ironmongery and 14.3 small ironmongery with notes and auxiliaries for nails, screws, springs, hooks, hinges; 14.7 tools with auxiliaries for drills, saws, knives; 14.11 ladders with auxiliaries for single/double/stepladders; 15.1 machines for industry and 15.3 machines for household use). Notes call out inclusions/exclusions (e.g., power drills are in 14.7.12; door closers included in 15.1.25; kitchen machines elsewhere in 11.1.10; washing machines in 13.3.23). Use principal vs. auxiliary sections to select the most specific classification available, and follow the notes to avoid common misplacements.
